Subject: Re: Discovery — Paybridge / Redwood (quick follow-up)

Thanks for the demo today, Dylan. Appreciate the overview — a few quick clarifying items we discussed on the call: 

- Volume profile: we roughly expect 10M inference tokens/month to start (chat prompts + assistant responses). Peak QA/test months could go to ~20M tokens.
- Feature mix: ~60% generation/chat, ~30% embeddings for semantic search, ~10% reranking/summary.
- SLO: 200–300ms p95 for user-interactive features; some background jobs can tolerate 1–2s.

Budget side: our finance lead asked for a target ballpark of cost/unit to evaluate feasibility. We need an estimate in $/1M tokens (monthly) and expected monthly spend bands so procurement can route appropriately. For procurement thresholds: anything >$50k/month will need an RFP + legal review; anything >$15k/month will require PO + standard SOW.

Can you provide a concise cost breakdown (target $/1M tokens for our mix, plus what a 10M and 20M month would look like) so I can pass to Linda and procurement?

Thanks — Alex
Product Lead, Paybridge

Alex — thanks again for the call. Per your ask, see a concise estimate below (high-level, assumes Redwood hosted API with modest batching + prefix caching):

Summary unit economics (estimated) — Paybridge workload mix (60% chat gen, 30% embeddings, 10% rerank):
- Target blended cost: $225 per 1M tokens (this is our suggested planning number for chat-heavy workloads with caching/quantization gains).
- Embeddings priced differently (per embedding unit) — included here as blended into the above for simplicity; details in attached spreadsheet.

Monthly spend bands (blended estimate):
- 10M tokens/mo -> ~$2,250/month
- 20M tokens/mo -> ~$4,500/month
- 50M tokens/mo -> ~$11,250/month (note: at scale we recommend a dedicated capacity quote which reduces unit cost ~30–45%)

Procurement thresholds (Paybridge constraints you noted):
- < $15k/month: standard PO + SOW (self-serve onboarding possible)
- $15k–$50k/month: procurement + legal review required; typically we move to a committed Dedicated capacity offering for predictable pricing
- > $50k/month: enterprise contracting cycle (RFP, legal SLA negotiation).

Next steps I recommend:
1) I’ll attach a simple token-expectation workbook (see attachment) mapping usage patterns to monthly spend.
2) Marissa will prepare a Dedicated capacity estimation if you want to model committed vs on-demand economics (Rishi, can you draft?).
3) If procurement needs a ballpark MSA/SOW for internal routing, we can share a redline-friendly template — let me know who to send to (Linda?).

Quick questions for you: can you confirm the 10M baseline is the expected go-live run-rate (or is that a first-quarter average)? Also, is there a procurement lead for Paybridge who needs the initial numbers in a one-pager?

Attaching: paybridge_token_estimate.xlsx (workbook) and redwood_pricing_summary.pdf

Best,
Dylan

Thanks for the context. Quick Dedicated sensitivity (back-of-envelope):
- Hosted (no commit): blended $225 / 1M tokens (as Dylan said) — good for low to mid volume and fast time-to-value.
- Committed Dedicated (50M tokens/mo commitment): estimated blended $140 / 1M tokens -> ~$7,000/month effective for 50M commit.
- Larger committed profile (200M tokens/mo): estimated blended $95 / 1M tokens (we’d likely propose custom infra/quotas + SLA adjustments).

Procurement artifacts to attach:
- Standard MSA (editable)
- SOC 2 Type II attestation summary (PDF)
- Data processing addendum (DPA)
- Example SOW for Dedicated capacity (term, support SLAs, billing cadence)

Notes on timing and routing:
- If Paybridge is under $15k/mo expected spend, they can proceed with a PO and standard onboarding (no enterprise legal required).
- For ~$15k–$50k/mo we usually require procurement + legal 1–2 week review for standard redlines; Dedicated quoting begins in parallel.
- >$50k/mo: expect 2–6 week procurement + legal cycle depending on redlines and security questionnaires.

I uploaded a short Dedicated sensitivity sheet into the attached workbook. Alex — let me know if you want me to join a call with Linda/procurement to walk the finance/comparison slide for stakeholders.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
